source.title: Optimization Variance: Exploring Generalization Properties of DNNs
source.authors: Xiao Zhang; Dong-Rui Wu; Haoyi Xiong; Bo Dai

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether widening a network is associated with better test performance, using a ResNet width sweep and optimization variance rather than the one-hidden-layer ReLU setup in V2.
record.gate_note: The paper does not report random-label memorization, training error at each width, or whether the widths exceed the interpolation threshold. Its main bias-variance and optimization-variance results concern epoch-wise behavior, which no listed version directly names.
record.test_reason: The width sweep measures test accuracy but never establishes zero training error or which widths exceed the width needed to fit. It therefore cannot test V2's defining claim about widening past that point. Optimization variance and epoch-wise double descent measure different constructs from the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that variance dominates their observed epoch-wise double descent, and that training-set OV tracks test-error changes and enables early stopping without a validation set. They also report improving accuracy with ResNet18 width, while explicitly acknowledging weak OV–accuracy correlation across substantially different architectures.
record.recipe_differences: The width sweep uses ResNet18 rather than one-hidden-layer ReLU networks and does not report zero training error or the interpolation threshold. The broader study measures bias, variance, and optimization variance over training epochs.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that OV and test accuracy did not show strong cross-model correlation when comparing substantially different architectures, such as VGG and ResNet.

fits_no_version.finding: In the ResNet18 CIFAR10 sweep, wider networks generally achieve better test accuracy and lower OV; OV and test accuracy correlate at −0.94 (p = 0.0006). Training errors are not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing ResNet18 width improves held-out accuracy within this tested 100-epoch recipe, without establishing whether the widths interpolate the training data.

fits_no_version.finding: OV generally tracks test performance over training and enables early stopping with test errors close to stopping based on test accuracy. Its correlation does not extend reliably across substantially different architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-set optimization variance can indicate changes in test performance within a training run and some architecture families.

record.problems: The width sweep reports no training errors, so it does not locate the interpolation threshold. Test-accuracy values by width are presented in a figure rather than enumerated in the text. The authors report no strong cross-model OV/test-accuracy correlation across substantially different architectures.
record.rows_left_out: No other row reports a result on the listed claim versions. The paper's epoch-wise loss, bias, variance, and OV findings do not directly measure a behavior named by V1 or V3–V8; the relevant general finding is recorded under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe; chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Whether test error continues falling as width increases beyond the width needed to reach zero training error; convergence and the interpolation threshold are not established.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under comparable tuning budgets. Multiple optimizers are used to examine OV, without establishing the claimed optimizer comparison.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their performance difference.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness versus generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. OV measures variation in logits after batch-dependent updates.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Failure to establish the interpolation threshold is an evidence gap, not a result limiting or challenging V2. The supplied text provides no additional result that directly tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test performance for the same architectures and recipes.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks, MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10, zero training error, and whether the tested widths are beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons under the stated tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.size_stated: For each convolutional layer, filters set to k/4 times the original model, k = 1, 2, ..., 8
rows.operation_detail: Widened each convolutional layer across eight filter-width settings; trained on CIFAR10 with no label noise.
rows.value: As k increases, test accuracy increases; Pearson correlation coefficient between OV and test accuracy reached −0.94 (p = 0.0006).
rows.note: The paper states the trend and correlation but does not give per-width accuracy values in the text. It does not report training error or establish that widths are beyond the interpolation threshold.
rows.check: The reported improvement with width does not establish improvement beyond the interpolation threshold. Missing training-error measurements make V2 unassessable, rather than partially observed. The reported r = −0.94 (p = 0.0006) measures OV versus test accuracy, not width versus test accuracy. Training used Adam; SGD was used only to calculate OV.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet18 width sweep on CIFAR10, k = 1, 2, ..., 8
reader_labels.reason: Test accuracy increases with width in the reported sweep (R1), consistent with continued generalization, though the interpolation threshold is not established.
